title: The Complete Guide to Choosing a Cannabis Dispensary POS System
summary: How to choose a cannabis dispensary POS: the features that matter, the questions to ask, and the pitfalls to avoid — plus a downloadable 12-point scorecard.
body_markdown:
Choosing a dispensary POS comes down to scoring every vendor on the same twelve criteria before you sign: compliance automation, uptime, real total cost, support, contract terms, all-in-one coverage, payments, inventory, delivery, hardware, data ownership, and reporting. Score each from 1 to 5, then compare totals.


A Point of Sale (POS) system is the most critical piece of software a dispensary runs: the central hub for sales, compliance, inventory management, and customer data. Running a dispensary is complex, but choosing the system that runs it should not be.


**This guide walks through the features that matter, the questions to ask vendors, the pitfalls that cost operators money, and a 12-point scorecard you can use to compare systems side by side.**

## Key Takeaways


- The twelve criteria that decide a dispensary POS purchase are compliance automation, uptime and reliability, pricing transparency, support model, contract terms, all-in-one coverage, payments, inventory management, delivery support, hardware flexibility, data ownership, and reporting.
- Compliance automation, uptime, and real total cost are deal-breakers rather than trade-offs. A low score on any one of the three should eliminate a vendor regardless of its total score.
- Per-transaction, per-user, and per-feature fees mean your POS cost climbs as your sales grow, so compare the total annual cost of everything you will actually use instead of the advertised monthly rate.
- Contract terms and data ownership decide whether you can leave a system that stops working for you. Month-to-month terms and free data export are the two clauses to confirm in writing before signing.
- Run the demo on your own scenarios, not the vendor's. A 4/20 rush, a delivery run, and a Metrc discrepancy will tell you more than any feature list.


---


## Why Choosing the Right POS Matters


A cannabis POS system does more than process transactions: it touches every part of your operation. From state compliance reporting to inventory accuracy to how long a customer waits at the counter, the right system can help you:


- Stay compliant with state Track and Trace requirements
- Support multiple sales channels and flexible retail models, including in-store, delivery, pickup, curbside, lounges, and events
- Manage and sync inventory accurately across all sales channels
- Improve customer experiences with personalized service
- Increase efficiency by reducing clicks and staff training time
- Avoid costly compliance errors and audits


---


## Key Features to Look for in a Cannabis POS System


Seven feature areas separate a dispensary POS that carries your operation from one your team works around every day: compliance, inventory, sales flexibility, data, loyalty, reliability, and user experience.


### 1. Compliance and Metrc Integration


Compliance is non-negotiable in cannabis retail, so compliance automation is the first thing to evaluate in any dispensary POS. Your POS system should:


- Sync real-time sales data with Metrc, or batch report at the end of the day, depending on regulation in your market
- Track inventory changes across all sales channels
- Manage returns and exchanges, including tax, inventory, and vendor credits
- Offer built-in tools to catch errors before they reach state regulators

### 2. Inventory Management


Accurate inventory keeps your dispensary profitable, and inventory data is what your compliance reporting and your tax position both rest on. Look for:


- Real-time inventory tracking across sales channels (in-store, delivery, pickup)
- Low-stock alert emails and filters, plus expiring product tracking
- Vendor management and purchase order creation
- Easy-to-use cycle counting tools to reduce shrinkage and inventory discrepancies


SKU-level inventory data also drives the cost accounting behind your tax position. See how COGS works in our[guide to Schedule III and what it means for dispensary taxes](https://getmeadow.com/blog/cannabis-schedule-III) .


### 3. Sales Flexibility and Omnichannel Support


Your POS should let you sell wherever your customers are, without a second system bolted on for each channel. Key features include:


- In-store, delivery, and pickup support within a single system
- Built-in dynamic delivery and hub-and-spoke delivery models
- Flexible retail models, including lounges, kiosks, packing rooms, and floating sales


See how PleasureMed runs in-store retail, delivery, and a cannabis lounge as one experience on Meadow. ➡️ **[Read the Case Study](https://getmeadow.com/blog/pleasuremed-case-study)**


### 4. Data and Analytics


A dispensary POS should turn daily sales into decisions you can act on this week, not reports you export and ignore. A strong system offers:


- Easily customizable sales reports and dashboards
- Performance tracking down to the specific product, brand, category, or special
- Customer data you can segment to personalize marketing
- Sales forecasting and low stock alerts


### 5. Customer Loyalty and Marketing Tools


Repeat customers carry a dispensary's margin, so loyalty and customer data belong in the POS rather than in a separate tool your budtenders never open. Look for:


- Customer profiles that show budtenders past purchases, preferences, and notes
- Integrated loyalty programs with customizable rewards
- Ability to segment customers for targeted promotions
- Menu and SEO tools that help your store show up in local search


Once your loyalty program is running, the next lever is online visibility. ### 6. Reliability and Uptime


A POS outage stops your dispensary from selling, so treat reliability as a deal-breaker rather than a trade-off. Ask about:


- Uptime history and reliability statistics (Meadow has maintained 99.99% uptime since 2014, including 100% uptime every 4/20)
- A consistent record of uptime on 4/20 and other peak sales periods

An intuitive POS reduces staff errors and shortens training, which shows up directly in checkout times and turnover costs. Ensure:


- Simple, intuitive interfaces for budtenders and managers
- Fast workflows (fewer clicks, fast load times)

## The 12-Point Cannabis POS Scorecard


The fastest way to compare dispensary POS systems is to score every vendor from 1 to 5 on the same twelve criteria, then compare totals. Here is the full scorecard:


# Criterion What a 5 looks like


1 Compliance automation Real-time, automatic track-and-trace sync, with error-catching before the state sees it


2 Uptime and reliability Documented uptime history and a clean record on 4/20 and peak days


3 Pricing transparency One flat monthly fee instead of per-transaction, per-user, or per-feature fees; same price as you grow


4 Support model Free and unlimited support with fast, measured response times, not per-ticket billing


5 Contract terms Month-to-month, no annual lock-in


6 All-in-one coverage POS, eCommerce, delivery, loyalty, and payments in one system, not stitched vendors


7 Payments Debit, ACH, dual pricing, and cashless options, native rather than bolted on


8 Inventory management Real-time tracking, SKU-level cost, cycle counts, and audit support, which also drives accurate COGS


9 Delivery support Routing, live tracking, compliant manifests, and hub-and-spoke models


10 Hardware flexibility Runs on hardware you already have, no forced purchase


11 Data ownership Free export, so your data comes with you if you leave


12 Reporting and analytics Real-time sales, inventory, and customer insight in one place


**Scoring guidance:** Compliance, uptime, and real cost are deal-breakers, not trade-offs. A low score on any one of those three should knock a vendor out, regardless of the total. Criterion 3 is where most of the surprises hide, so price the total annual cost of everything you will actually use. Our breakdown of[what dispensaries actually pay for cannabis POS](https://getmeadow.com/blog/cannabis-pos-pricing) covers the fee structures that do not show up on a pricing page.

**How to evaluate:** Run a live demo with your real scenarios, such as a 4/20 rush, a delivery run, and a Metrc discrepancy. Ask for references from dispensaries your size. Price the total annual cost, not the sticker price. And test support response time before you sign.

## Questions to Ask When Evaluating Cannabis POS Systems


These questions surface what a demo will not: how the vendor makes money, what happens if you leave, and who owns your data.


- How does the POS provider make money? Are there hidden fees that my customers or my business pay?
- Can you leave the contract at any time if the system does not meet your needs, or are you locked into an annual or biannual auto-renewing contract?
- How does the system handle compliance with Metrc or other state systems? Does it allow negative packages?
- Are you locked into a specific payment processor, and which cashless payment options does the system support natively?
- What integrations are available (Weedmaps, QuickBooks, OnFleet, and others)?
- What kind of customer support is available, and what is the measured response time? Ask for the number, not an adjective.
- How easily can you switch from your current system? Our[dispensary POS migration guide](https://getmeadow.com/blog/dispensary-pos-migration) covers how to switch without losing a day of sales.
- What is their history of uptime, including performance on the busiest days like 4/20?
- Who owns the company, and what are their values?
- Who owns, and who can sell, your data?


---


## Common Pitfalls to Avoid


The most expensive dispensary POS mistakes are made before the contract is signed, and all four below are avoidable in the evaluation stage.


- **Choosing based on price alone.** Cheap POS systems often lead to expensive compliance mistakes, lost sales during downtime, and costly workarounds. Many make up a low base rate with hidden fees or pay-per-feature billing.
- **Overlooking scalability.** Confirm the system can support growth without a platform switch later. Manual entry becomes a bottleneck fast.
- **Ignoring compliance protections.** Verify accurate Metrc syncing and error-fixing tools, not just a Metrc logo on the website.
- **Underestimating support.** Choose a provider with a proven record of fast, knowledgeable service, and test it during the sales process.

## Common Questions


### How do I choose a dispensary POS system?


Score every vendor from 1 to 5 on the same twelve criteria: compliance automation, uptime, pricing transparency, support model, contract terms, all-in-one coverage, payments, inventory management, delivery support, hardware flexibility, data ownership, and reporting. Then run a live demo with your real scenarios and check references from dispensaries your size. Treat compliance, uptime, and real cost as pass-or-fail rather than scored items.


### Does a dispensary POS need to integrate with Metrc?


In Metrc states, yes. Your POS should sync sales and inventory changes with Metrc automatically, in real time or via end-of-day batch reporting, and catch errors before they reach state regulators. Manual Metrc entry is one of the most common sources of compliance violations, fines, and license suspensions.


### How much does a dispensary POS system cost?


Pricing models vary more than sticker prices do. Some vendors charge one flat monthly fee; others layer on per-transaction fees, per-ticket support charges, hardware purchases, and integration fees. Compare the total annual cost across everything you will actually use, not the advertised monthly rate. Our[cannabis POS pricing guide](https://getmeadow.com/blog/cannabis-pos-pricing) breaks down each model.


### Can I switch dispensary POS systems without losing data?


Yes. A well-planned migration moves your product catalog, customer profiles, and inventory counts, and a good vendor manages the switch so you do not lose a day of sales. Our[dispensary POS migration guide](https://getmeadow.com/blog/dispensary-pos-migration) walks through the process step by step.

The best dispensary POS is the one that scores highest for your state, your sales channels, and the twelve criteria above.
